---
title: Negative claims
description: Observe prose claims or deliver library-written typed statements, with the search scope and gaps preserved.
---

`.negativeClaims()` has two forms. `{ prose: true }` observes ordinary answers and
files warnings. `{ field, tools, unestablished }` makes the library write typed
negative statements from cited searches. Prose observation never verifies or
withholds an answer. Typed enforcement is **available, not recommended** until its
benchmark gates pass. Offline replays are diagnostic; structured-path accuracy and
usefulness remain **unmeasured**.

## Observe an ordinary answer

No output schema, citation field, tool-name list or answer validator is required.
Native tool dispatch records supply the observations; assistant messages and
summaries never become evidence. The example's local search declares a source gap,
then the mock model makes a broader claim.

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/111-negative-prose-observe.ts"
  region="observe"
  title="Observe a warning and deliver the unchanged answer"
/>

The prose-only arm adds no correction request or delivery buffer. It preserves
normal streaming, and the returned answer, final event, history and memory use
the same delivered text. It observes the terminal answer after output middleware;
it does not rewrite the answer, call a tool again or turn a warning into a veto.
An independent `.outputSchema()` or `.answerValidation()` retains its own behavior,
including retries, buffering and refusal. `.outputFallback()` is refused with
the prose-only arm because a fallback can replace an answer after observation.

The English grammar is a **heuristic**. The prior detector **failed every free-replay
benchmark gate**; the revised, data-anchored path remains **unmeasured**.
It can miss negatives and flag correct statements. Comparing a claim with read evidence requires an anchor in
the same clause: a dispatched read's declared `said` words, actual sent value or
resolved name or alias. Host-only and kept-out values cannot supply that anchor;
another clause or a user message cannot supply evidence. Anchoring permits an
observation, not a binding or proof. Entity resolution and coverage checks remain
separate, so a sent name can still produce `entity-unresolved`.

If the grammar detects an eligible negative and no dispatched native read is
recorded for the current turn, the observer files one `negative-claim-note` with
code `no-read` per answer, within the observation budgets below. For example,
answering "Payments has no incidents. There are no incidents anywhere." without a
recorded read produces one warning. A read from an earlier turn does not suppress
it. A recorded dispatched read does suppress this note even if it failed or its
result was kept out; that presence check does not establish usable evidence.
Because the ledger can be incomplete, `no-read` does not prove that no read occurred.

The observer filters the exact normalized ordinary clauses "None.", "No action
is needed." and "Tests: 0 failed."; they produce no `no-read` warning. Added words or a
separate negative clause remain eligible. The note records missing read evidence;
it never verifies, blocks or rewrites the answer.

`agent.findings()` retains `negative-claim` and `negative-claim-note` rows. A
current-turn row makes the assessment not-sure with reason
`negative-prose-unverified`, including a detected claim with no coverage note.
**No finding does not mean verified.** The observer is not an exhaustive proof
that the answer is true.

Subscribe to `agentfootprint.findings.negative_claim` before running the agent.
It emits once per claim or unread-unit row, with `kind`, field and span,
phrase-pack version, iteration and turn, and either claim/note codes with native
result references or an unread-unit `code`. Answer text, candidate labels and tool
values are excluded. Metadata is bounded; `truncated: true` means that metadata
was shortened or references omitted. The typed arm emits the same warnings.

Observation examines at most 65,536 UTF-16 code units across 256 string values,
with at most 32 detected claims and unjudged units combined. One shared work
budget also bounds pattern preparation and evidence/name matching across all
fields; exhausting it produces one `input-limit` note and discards partial findings.
An oversized or
unreadable structured input, or a field path over 4,096 code units, produces an
`input-limit` note; too many units produce `too-many-claims`. Each replaces partial
findings with one whole-answer note. Recognized code and unsupported-language
units produce `in-code-block` or `language-unsupported` notes. Language detection
uses a closed heuristic and can miss non-English text; it is not multilingual
verification. `strictProse` and `enforceProse` remain unavailable.

### Add literal phrases

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/111-negative-prose-observe.ts"
  region="custom-phrases"
  title="Optional app phrases for the same observer"
/>

`NegativeClaimPhraseExtensions` describes the optional `phrases` object.
Pass this configuration to `.negativeClaims(customObservation)`. At most 32 phrases total
may extend `none` and `complete`, with at most 128 UTF-16 code units each. They are
literal words, not regexes, slot patterns or executable predicates. Extensions use
the same language, code, anchoring and budget rules. Their frozen effective pack
has its own hash in the reported version; adding phrases never enables enforcement.

## Deliver typed negative statements

The model supplies `restsOn` result handles. The library derives the claim type and
searched subject from the admitted result records, then writes the scope, gaps and
delivered statement. Model wording never selects the subject or supplies evidence.

`NegativeClaimsOptions` configures the field, eligible tools and failure behavior.
`NegativeClaimCitation` is the model-input shape; `DeliveredNegative` adds the
library's statement and version. `agent.answerNegatives()` returns the
`AnswerNegatives` metadata with per-source checked counts, diagnostics and
dispatched action outcomes; an action outcome does not prove an external effect.

Other fields remain unchecked model text. Prose observation is automatic beside
the typed arm; do not combine `prose: true` with `field`, `tools` or `unestablished`.
Either form accepts the optional literal `phrases` extension.

## Declare the search and bind the caller

Use a local tool with a [search declaration](/docs/build/tools#coverage-composed-from-the-call--search).
The declaration must describe the query the tool actually runs. Fill caller scope
through `hostFilled` from the host's authenticated identity, rather than asking the
model to supply it. A local `absent({ among })` result can also support a named miss.
MCP and ToolProvider declarations cannot establish a typed negative.

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/110-negative-claims.ts"
  region="search"
  title="A caller-scoped search with an explicit source gap"
/>

An empty result is different from an unread search: a completed search can find
zero rows. Missing observations, skipped checks and missing caller scope remain
unverified. A declaration that misdescribes the backend is outside this check's
guarantee; declarations and the host's identity are the trusted inputs.

## Give the model a citation field

The field must be a required top-level array. Each entry requires `kind` and
`restsOn`. The kind selects the claim to verify; optional `about` names its subject. Supply
`jsonSchema` explicitly or use a parser that provides
`toJsonSchema()`; the library does not infer a shape by executing a parser.

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/110-negative-claims.ts"
  region="schema"
  title="The model supplies citations, without statement text"
/>

The library serves the short-handle pattern `^r[1-9][0-9]{0,3}$`, limits the field
to 32 claims and each citation to 16 reads, and closes each entry to extra fields.
The model receives handles such as `r1` beside admitted results. Provider call IDs
never select evidence. Each read must be within the admitted caller scope. The
checker compares other reads using the cited searches' recorded subjects and
populations, so an unrelated model label cannot hide contradicting results.

| Requested kind | What the cited reads must establish                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `none`         | A declared absence within the composed search scope.                                                                                      |
| `not-found`    | A named miss from `absent({ among })`, with the inventory's limits.                                                                       |
| `complete`     | Completeness for the executed arguments, without an open page, reached cap or partial result. The statement describes rows actually read. |

### Evidence interpretation and existing parsers

The model's kind selects the proposition. `none` and `not-found` can be normalized
to the appropriate absence spelling only when every cited read explicitly declares
absence. A negative against returned rows is blocked, even if that read is complete.
The library never turns a negative into a complete-list claim. A changed absence
spelling gets an audit-only `absence-kind-normalized` note.

`complete` must be requested explicitly and satisfy the recorded completeness
declaration and every completeness guard. Proving an absence alone does not establish
completeness. Explicit completeness evidence can cover a zero-row search; a bare
empty list cannot supply it. For a failed complete-list claim whose narrower absence independently
passes all checks, the fallback says: "The requested complete-list claim is not
established; only this absence is." It retains every gap and the failed complete-list
verdict. Default `withhold` still withholds the answer; `state-searched` may deliver
this explicit fallback. It never gets `as-checked`.

A raw empty list, failed read or missing coverage never becomes declared absence.
A known native empty read without an absence declaration is reported as
`undeclared-empty`, without minting evidence or treating it as a citation typo.
Multiple reads retain their individual scopes; the library does not invent a union.

When `about` is supplied, it must contain every cited read's public population value
as a complete name or identifier after the library's normalization. "Open incidents
for payments" matches a payments search; "payments" cannot label a billing search,
and `pay` does not match `payments`. Unknown or all-population values cannot be
validated against a supplied phrase. This checks name inclusion, not the meaning of
surrounding prose. The original phrase is never delivered as the subject.

Keep `kind` and `restsOn` required in both your parser and JSON Schema. `about` may
remain required by your app or be omitted. The library does not rewrite an opaque
parser or invent values to satisfy it. Surrounding answer prose remains unchecked.

## Deliver the statement and its marker together

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/110-negative-claims.ts"
  region="configure"
  title="Deliver the library statement"
/>

An established entry gains its checked `kind`, `statement`, `delivery: 'record-composed'`
and `version`. Display that marker beside the sentence. Delivered `about` is the single
public population value from the admitted search, never the model's phrase. It is
omitted for multiple or unavailable subjects; the statement keeps each read's scope.
Host-only identity values never become subject labels. The answer-level delivery is
`as-checked` only when its sole field consists of established library statements.
Other model fields make delivery `recorded`; this never verifies surrounding prose.
The model-input parser describes only
citations; `runTyped()` returns the enriched delivered object without running that
parser over it again.

Every execution mode delivers the library statement, including when an app's
`.answerValidation()` uses observe mode. The final answer is buffered so a draft
cannot escape through streaming. The person, `turn_end.answerNegatives`, conversation
history and memory receive the same statements and gaps.

`unestablished` chooses the failure behavior:

| Setting              | Delivery                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `withhold` (default) | Withhold the whole answer; the caller receives `AnswerValidationError`, HTTP hosts return 422 and AG-UI reports `RUN_ERROR`.                                      |
| `state-searched`     | Replace the entry with what the admitted record says was searched and any admitted contrary result. The failed or unverified standing stays failed or unverified. |

A contrary read is named by its result handle and shows bounded, quoted native
row values when they survived middleware, placement and truncation unchanged.
Otherwise its count is reported without re-exposing hidden values. A positive
result without a coverage declaration is explicitly labelled that way.

Complete statements count every admitted fact, series point and edge. They show
row identities only when all native rows survived the final tool-result boundary
unchanged; removing or replacing a collection suppresses those identities. These
statements use template version 7.

A bad citation gets one correction request naming valid handles, with no tools
available. If `.outputSchema()` enables retries, schema correction shares that
same one-request budget with citation and evidence correction, even when `retries`
is greater than one. Rejected drafts and correction instructions stay out of
conversation history and memory. A correction cannot repeat a write to satisfy
the checker. A later dispatched
call that may write invalidates an earlier read even if the call fails; a local
`effects: 'read'` declaration can identify a read-only tool. Remote read-only hints
cannot. Reads retained through a pause remain eligible within the same turn;
earlier-turn reads are stale and their refusal identifies the earlier turn and recorded date.

This does not verify the rest of an answer. An empty citation array makes no typed
claim. Every original free-form model string, including nested fields and `about`, is observed
before the library writes its statements. Detected negatives file `negative-claim`
findings; unread units file `negative-claim-note` findings. Both make the answer
fold not-sure, without changing delivery. The grammar has known false positives and
misses; prose remains unchecked even when it produces no finding.

The same whole-answer observation budgets described above apply.
The model is instructed to state negatives only through cited searches. These
instructions do not guarantee compliance.

Typed delivery introduced the global answer-account `templateVersion` 12,
including for agents without `.negativeClaims()`. The standalone prose arm retains
that version and the `negative-prose-unverified` assessment reason.

The checker compares other observations only within its declared subject and scope rules.
Independent host-authored answer checks continue to apply, and a library statement
never turns an unverified answer into a verified one.

Both mock examples run without credentials or network access:

```sh
npm run example -- examples/features/110-negative-claims.ts
npm run example -- examples/features/111-negative-prose-observe.ts
```
